metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: To repeatedly dwell on, calculate, or obsess over past events or grievances.
acceptable_visual_variants: A hand turning away from an abacus or a ledger book left open and untouched.
A person closing a book of old records or tallies and looking away.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing someone literally counting coins, stones, or tally marks on a wall, which suggests financial calculation or imprisonment rather than mental rumination.
metaphor_spans.tenor: Mentally revisiting and obsessing over past painful memories.
metaphor_spans.vehicle: Counting physical items or keeping a tally.
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a person looking at a chaotic, unquantifiable cloud of abstract shapes or shadows, resisting the urge to sort or count them.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: To revive or make painful memories feel raw and active again.
acceptable_visual_variants: A hand touching a cracked, dry surface that suddenly glows with hot, sharp light along the cracks.
A faded memory sketch suddenly gaining sharp, harsh outlines.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: To make fresh (like food, flowers, or a physical wound).
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing someone watering a plant or washing a physical wound, which carries positive or purely medical connotations rather than emotional self-harm.

metaphor_mapping.vehicle_concept: refreshing a physical state or wound

metaphor_spans.tenor: Re-awakening emotional pain so that it hurts as intensely as when it first happened.
metaphor_spans.vehicle: Refreshing or renewing a physical object or wound to keep it from healing or decaying.
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a heart or abstract emotional core glowing with a sharp, sudden red or orange light amidst a cool, dark background, symbolizing the sudden reignition of pain.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The idiomatic and rhythmic quality of the refrain 'जो बीत गई सो बात गई' (Jo beet gayi so baat gayi), which relies on internal rhyme and a proverbial cadence, is flattened into a literal English statement.
The translation of 'गिनते हैं' as 'count' misses the idiomatic Hindi sense of 'ginnā' in this context, which means to dwell on, obsessively recount, or keep score of past grievances.

A hand releasing a bird into the open sky, representing the liberating essence of life.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Showing someone writing the word 'Life' on a tag or label, which is overly literal and lacks emotional depth.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of 'भूल जाना नसीब है' as 'Is to forget what’s fated' alters the meaning. In Hindi, 'naseeb' refers to destiny or fortune; the original line suggests that being able to forget is a matter of good fortune or a gift of destiny, rather than forgetting destiny itself.

The colloquial, encouraging tone of 'जीने का है' (one must live / is about living) is rendered as 'what's awaited', which introduces a passive expectation not present in the active, forward-looking Hindi phrasing.

original_poem:
जो बीत गई सो बात गई,
उसी को फिर न गिनते हैं।
हर दर्द को ताजा करते,
हर ग़म को फिर से जीते हैं।

जीने का नाम है यारों,
भूल जाना नसीब है।
जो बीत गई सो बात गई,
आगे बढ़कर जीने का है।
poem_title: Jo Beet Gayi So Baat Gayi
translated_poem:
What is past, is past,
We do not count that again.
Each pain is made fresh,
Every sorrow we live again.

The name of living, dear friends,
Is to forget what’s fated.
What is past, is past,
Moving on is what’s awaited.
